summary: Nariaki Nakazato is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1966–1976). He held posts at Kobe University, the Centre for East Asian Cultural Studies, and the University of Tokyo (~1996–2010).
Narimoto Tamayama was a Buddhist studies and Japanology scholar. He served as a professor at Taisho University, where his posts were attested in 1974 and 1988.

Philosopher Natalie Depraz studied at ENS de lettres et sciences humaines, St. Sergius Institute, and Paris Nanterre University. She held posts at the Collège international de philosophie, Paris-Sorbonne University, and the University of Rouen-Normandy.
Natalie Gummer is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. She was affiliated with Harvard University (attested 2001) and became a professor of religious studies at Beloit College in 2001.

Natalie Maxwell is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar. She earned her PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison under Stephan Beyer, also studying with Geshe Wangyal, Khensur Ngawang Lekden, Geshe Lhundub Sopa, and Minoru Kiyota.
Historian Natalie Rothman studied at the University of Michigan from 1999 to 2006. She took up a post at the University of Toronto in 2006 and taught Matthew King.

Natasha Heller is a scholar of Sinology and Buddhist studies who earned her PhD from Harvard University. She was a postdoctoral fellow at UC Berkeley (attested 2008) and an assistant professor at UCLA (attested 2016).

Natasha Reichle, a scholar of history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies, completed her dissertation at UC Berkeley under Joanna Gottfried Williams. She also studied under Amin Sweeney, Lewis Lancaster, Patricia Berger, Jeffrey Hadler, and Ninik Lunde.
Natasja Bosma is an Indology scholar who completed her PhD at the University of Groningen under the supervision of Hans T. Bakker between circa 2011 and 2018.

Nathan Sivin, a scholar of Sinology and history, studied at MIT, Defense Language Institute, and Harvard. He held posts at MIT, the University of Pennsylvania (~1977–2006), and Chinese Academy of Sciences (~1994).

Nathan W. Hill studied at Harvard under Leonard van der Kuijp and Jay Jasanoff. A scholar of Tibetology and linguistics, he held posts at SOAS University of London (~2008–2019) and Trinity College Dublin (2021).
Nathaniel Brassey Halhed was an Indology and linguistics scholar who studied at Harrow School. He served as an official for the East India Company from circa 1771 to 1785.
Nathaniel DeWitt Garson is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Virginia under Jeffrey Hopkins, having also studied under Khenpo Namdrol.

Nathmal Tatia was a scholar of Indology, philosophy, and religious studies who earned a DLitt at the University of Calcutta under Satkari Mookerjee and Sukhlal Sanghvi. He was director of the Jain Vishva Bharati Institute (attested 1982–1990).
Navina Lamminger is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD at Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich under the supervision of Franz-Karl Ehrhard.

Nawang Tsering Shakspo is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar who studied under doctoral supervisor Lal Mani Joshi. He held a post as a lecturer at the Central Institute of Buddhist Studies (attested 1985).
Neal Arvid Donner is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Sinology who studied at the University of British Columbia, where he was taught by Leon Hurvitz (attested 1976).
Ng-Fung Yuen is a Buddhist and religious studies scholar who earned a PhD at the University of the West under the supervision of Kottegoda S. Warnasuriya (attested 2009).
Ngan-che Chan is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD at the University of Hong Kong under doctoral supervisor Jing Yin, having also studied under K. L. Dhammajoti.

Ngawang Jinpa was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied at Drepung Loseling Monastery. He taught Kevin A. Vose and Samdhong Rinpoche, and served as a professor at St. Joseph's College, Darjeeling (attested 1995).
